name: Baylo
og: A community bartering app for Barangay Balibago. I built the web platform and its backend; 100 respondents rated it 4.89/5.
summary: A community bartering app for Barangay Balibago, Santa Rosa, Laguna, built by our team of four. I was the only web developer and built the whole web platform on my own; my three teammates built the mobile app. In the mobile app, residents post items, chat and trade with their neighbours, and Gemini estimates each item's value and finds good trade matches.

score.text: from 100 respondents in the ISO/IEC 25010 evaluation I led

shots.alt: Baylo home page with the Baylo logo over a record shop photo and a row of categories
shots.caption: The home page: search, categories and the app download.

shots.alt: Baylo listings page with filters, trending items and recently added items
shots.caption: Browsing listings, with filters for condition and price, and matches.

shots.alt: The Baylo team and our adviser at the capstone presentation, with the title slide behind us
shots.caption: Presenting Baylo with my team at FEU Alabang.

mission: Baylo is our capstone at FEU Alabang. It lets residents of Barangay Balibago discover, swap and share items with their neighbours.

We were a team of four. We planned the system together, from research and wireframes to the final design. My teammates built the mobile app. I built the web platform and its backend on my own, and led the research and evaluation.

roles.title: Web platform
roles.text: built Baylo's web platform alone: a FastAPI backend with 9 route modules over a 13-table PostgreSQL database, and a React, TypeScript and Tailwind web app where residents browse and search listings and barangay officials monitor activity in the admin dashboard. Trading happens in the mobile app.

roles.title: AI features
roles.text: built and tested the AI value estimate, matching and real-time notifications on the web first, then moved the final versions into the mobile app. With Gemini, it estimates an item's value and category from its photos, screens listings for prohibited items, and scores how well two items match for a trade (value, category, condition, interest).

roles.title: Real-time features
roles.text: wired up Firebase for sign-in, real-time chat and notifications.

roles.title: Admin tools
roles.text: built an admin dashboard for users, listings, reports and trades.

roles.title: Deployment
roles.text: deployed the backend to Google Cloud Run in a Docker container.

roles.title: Teamwork
roles.text: planned the system with the team, from research and wireframes to the final design, and kept the web and mobile sides in step as features changed. Both apps share one backend and Firebase, so accounts, listings, chat and notifications match on web and mobile.

roles.title: Research and evaluation
roles.text: led the survey and the ISO/IEC 25010 evaluation; 100 respondents rated the platform 4.89/5.

roles.title: Presentation
roles.text: presented and defended Baylo with the team at our capstone presentation.

arch.label: AI
arch.text: Google Gemini API for item value, category, screening and trade matching

arch.label: Hosting
arch.text: Web app on Firebase Hosting; backend in a Docker container on Google Cloud Run

name: LakbayWise
og: An AI-powered trip itinerary planner that supports accessibility, starting in Calamba and growing across Laguna.
summary: LakbayWise is an AI-powered trip itinerary planner that supports accessibility. Tell it where you're staying and what you enjoy, and it builds each day as a timed route that starts and ends at your stay.
detail: Every stop shows its wheelchair access, with a plain warning when it hasn't been checked. You can remove a stop, add places near your route, and share or print the plan. I'm starting in Calamba and growing across Laguna; the AI step is planned for later.

shots.alt: LakbayWise's home page: the headline "Plan a day in Laguna" over a photo of a red car on a country road, with a search bar for where you're staying, arrival and leaving dates and who is going
shots.caption: The home page: where you're staying, your dates and who is going.

shots.alt: The Plan your trip form with the stay, dates and group size filled in, a budget of 10,000 pesos, and a summary card beside it with a Plan my trip button
shots.caption: The five-step form, with a live summary of the trip.

shots.alt: A two-day plan from Hotel Marciano with Share and Print buttons, trip details, day tabs, a summary of stops, driving time and food cost, a note about rush hour, and a morning stop with an access label, beside a map of the route
shots.caption: A planned day: stops by morning, afternoon and evening, drive times, costs, access labels and the route map.

shots.alt: The end of a day's plan with a dinner stop that warns it has no step-free access information, then a More places near your route section with filters and cards that can be added to the morning, afternoon or evening
shots.caption: After the plan: add more places near the route, or remove a stop and undo it.

mission: Trip sites give everyone the same list of places and leave you to work out the drive between them. LakbayWise is an AI-powered trip itinerary planner that supports accessibility. It starts from where you're staying and builds each day in one area, so you spend the day at places and less of it in traffic.

It is made for travellers who need to know about access before they go. It shows wheelchair access where it is known, flags places where it isn't, and only plans places it has data for. My goal is the whole of Laguna, but I'm going one town at a time and starting with Calamba. For now it plans car trips.

roles.title: Planner
roles.text: built a rule-based planner that builds each day around one area: it centres the day on the best unused sight within about 3 km, splits it into morning, afternoon and evening, puts outdoor places early and at sunset, and places lunch and dinner at normal mealtimes. The same answers give the same plan.

roles.title: Accessibility
roles.text: let travellers say what access they need, and show each stop's wheelchair access and a note for rough terrain. Places with unknown access are still shown, with a clear warning; only places known to be inaccessible are left out. Access is never guessed.

roles.title: Drive times and costs
roles.text: added OSRM drive times with rush-hour factors, and a straight-line estimate when OSRM doesn't answer. Costs appear only where there is a basis, such as about ₱375 per person for a meal and from ₱800 for a hot spring, and every amount is labelled an estimate.

roles.title: Editing a plan
roles.text: built remove with undo, adding a place from "More places near your route" to the morning, afternoon or evening, the route map, and sharing a plan by link or printing it. A version check stops two browser tabs from overwriting each other.

roles.title: Website
roles.text: built the Nuxt 3, Vue 3 and TypeScript site: a landing page and a five-step form, with a Tailwind design system, a Leaflet map, light and dark mode, and a mock mode for designing without the backend. Typing what you like is matched to interests by keywords in English and Tagalog.

roles.title: Owner form
roles.text: built a form where business owners add their place. A person reviews every entry before anything is shown.

roles.title: Testing and CI
roles.text: wrote 102 backend tests and set up GitHub Actions to run the linter, the tests and a check that the website's types still match the API.

arch.label: Data
arch.text: SQLite, filled from a hand-checked list and OpenStreetMap places

arch.label: Routing
arch.text: OSRM for drive times, Nominatim to find the stay, with estimates as a fallback

arch.label: Shared types
arch.text: Made from the API's OpenAPI file, so the website and backend can't drift apart

arch.label: AI
arch.text: Designed in, switched off for the beta

score.text: pass in the backend, and CI checks that the website's types match the API

name: Wildwood
og: A cozy 3D browser game where you earn an animal's trust, plus the 3D website that opens it.
kind: Personal project, 3D browser game and its website
summary: A cozy 3D browser game where you earn an animal's trust instead of catching it, plus the 3D website I built for it, with a field guide, a map of the world and a button that opens the game. Farm by day, hold off wolf raids at night.

shots.alt: A dark 3D forest clearing with a campfire, mist and tall pines
shots.caption: The website's opening forest scene.

shots.alt: The field guide showing a 3D rusty knife with a list of weapons and its stats
shots.caption: The field guide, with day, dusk and night lighting.

shots.alt: A 3D map of the game world with forests, a creek, fields and clouds
shots.caption: The map of six regions.

shots.alt: Wildwood Farm title screen over the farm, with Play, How to play and Settings buttons
shots.caption: The game's title screen.

shots.alt: The player standing on the farm next to crop plots, with the hotbar, hearts and minimap on screen
shots.caption: In the game: hotbar, hearts, day clock and minimap.

mission: In Wildwood Farm you befriend animals instead of catching them. You offer the food an animal loves and stay still while its trust fills, and friends move into your barn and leave you gifts. Around that, you grow and cook crops, fish the creek, forge better weapons, and hold the farm through wolf raids at night.
The game needed a home page that feels like the game before anyone presses Play, so I built a website for it. It tells the story, shows what's in the world, and opens the game.

roles.title: Gameplay systems
roles.text: taming, farming (rain makes crops grow twice as fast), fishing with five fish that bite at different times and weather, cooking, and forging at the Blacksmith from enemy drops.

roles.title: Night raids
roles.text: programmed wolf raids that players fend off with gates, watchtowers and spike traps, with a morning report after each raid night.

roles.title: Walking buddy
roles.text: any barn animal can follow the player, dig up treats and warn about wolves.

roles.title: Controls and saves
roles.text: playable on keyboard, mouse or touch, with progress saved in the browser.

roles.title: Website rebuilt in Nuxt
roles.text: rebuilt the website with Nuxt 4, Vue 3 and GSAP: one component per section, prerendered to static HTML so the text shows straight away, with the 3D scenes loading right after in their own chunk.

roles.title: Website forest scene
roles.text: a 3D clearing with a smoking campfire, fireflies, ground mist, and a bunny and owl living there.

roles.title: Faster and sturdier 3D
roles.text: merged the hero's and the map's static props by material, so each frame needs about 185 draw calls instead of about 350 (hero) and 475 (map). A scene that throws is now dropped instead of freezing every 3D scene, resolution steps down when frames stay slow, and the map shows a list of regions when WebGL isn't available.

roles.title: Field guide and map
roles.text: weapons, animals and structures you can rotate and zoom under day, dusk and night lighting, and a 3D map of six regions where picking one flies the camera there.

arch.label: Website
arch.text: Nuxt 4 and Vue 3, prerendered to static HTML; one component per section

arch.label: 3D
arch.text: three.js r128 for both; the website's forest, field-guide viewer and world map are separate scenes in their own chunk, with bloom post-processing and orbit controls. Every model is built in code, so there are no model files to load

arch.label: Motion
arch.text: GSAP with ScrollTrigger on the website

arch.label: Game
arch.text: plain JavaScript in one index.html, no build step; progress saved in the browser's local storage

arch.label: Hosting
arch.text: GitHub Pages; the website is built and published by GitHub Actions
